rounds.proof_sketch: For input shape [128, 4000] with dim=1: outer_size=128, inner_size=1. Kernel launches with grid(128) and block(1), so outer_idx∈[0,127]. Original check 'outer_idx >= 128' is FALSE for all outer_idx in [0,127]. Mutated check 'outer_idx > 128' is also FALSE for all outer_idx in [0,127]. Both conditions evaluate identically (FALSE) for all valid thread indices.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary check from 'outer_idx >= outer_size' to 'outer_idx > outer_size'. This would only matter when outer_idx equals outer_size exactly. However, the CUDA kernel launch configuration uses grid(outer_size), which means blockIdx.x (assigned to outer_idx) ranges from 0 to outer_size-1 (i.e., 0 to 127 for this input). The value outer_idx=outer_size=128 is never reachable because CUDA grid indices are always strictly less than the grid dimension. Both the original and mutated conditions evaluate to FALSE for all launched threads, making the mutation semantically equivalent under this fixed configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mutation only affects behavior when outer_idx == outer_size, but this value is structurally unreachable given CUDA's grid indexing semantics (blockIdx.x ∈ [0, gridDim.x-1]). No value-level test can trigger this difference because it requires changing the tensor shape (which changes outer_size and thus the grid dimension) or using invalid CUDA semantics.
rounds.recommendations: Boundary-check mutations in CUDA kernels where the check compares thread indices against kernel-computed bounds are often equivalent when the launch configuration exactly matches the work size. Mutation testing tools should detect when relational operator changes affect unreachable predicates (where the variable's domain makes both operators evaluate identically) and mark such mutants as equivalent rather than requiring extensive testing.
